title: Traffic mirroring egress strategy + Terraform patterns (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft describing a conservative, observable-first approach to introducing traffic mirroring for egress flows in private (VPC / on-prem) deployments, while modernizing Terraform modules for NAT, private DNS, firewall layering, and Kubernetes network policies. Goal is to enable non-intrusive visibility into customer outbound traffic for debugging and audit without impacting SLOs.

Summary / TL;DR:
- Add an egress mirroring tier that samples 0.5–2% of flows to a deep-inspect observability cluster (no payload retention by default).
- Implement a fallback NAT proxy path for mirrored traffic to avoid disrupting production flows when mirroring sensors are overloaded.
- Refactor existing TF modules into three composable modules: network-egress, dns-handoff, and policy-layer.
- Rollout in canaries on two customers (staging-like and low-risk prod) with staged configs and telemetry gating.

Constraints and non-goals:
- This draft does NOT propose persistent packet capture for customer payloads. Retention and PII handling policies must be approved by security/legal before any payload capture is stored.
- Not covering on-prem air-gapped installations that disallow mirroring. Those deployments will follow a separate opt-out path.

High-level design:
1) Egress path (normal): pod -> node egress SNAT by cloud NAT -> internet
2) Egress path (mirrored sample): pod -> node eBPF mirror sampler -> mirror collector (internal VPC) -> optional deep-inspect cluster
3) Fallback: if mirror queue/backpressure detected, mirrored packet is dropped (no downstream effect) OR optionally proxied via NAT path so original flow continues unaffected.

Key components and responsibilities:
- Mirror sampler: eBPF program on hosts (or iptables TPROXY where eBPF not available) that samples by flow 1-in-N or probabilistic hash. Owned by eng-serving-runtime & SRE.
- Mirror collector: stateless receiver (k8s service) that receives mirrored copies over GRE/VXLAN or gRPC encapsulation. Owned by observability team.
- NAT fallback proxy: lightweight sidecar/proxy that preserves source IP semantics if mirror path is unavailable. Owned by platform-engineering.
- DNS handoff: Private DNS entries (split-horizon) that route collector.subnet.local -> mirror collector IPs in VPC. Owned by private-deployments team.
- TF modules: reusable modules that provision mirror subnets, IAM roles, firewall rules, and optional NAT proxies. Owned by infra/terraform.

Terraform module sketch (interface, not full code):
- module "network-egress" {
    source = "./modules/network-egress"
    vpc_id = var.vpc_id
    mirror_enabled = var.mirror_enabled
    mirror_sample_rate = var.mirror_sample_rate # e.g., 0.01 == 1%
    mirror_target = var.mirror_target_cidr
    nat_enabled = var.nat_enabled
    nat_gateway_ids = var.nat_gateway_ids
  }

- module "dns-handoff" {
    source = "./modules/dns-handoff"
    zone_id = var.private_zone_id
    collector_records = var.collector_records # list of IPs / hostnames
    split_horizon = var.split_horizon # bool
  }

- module "policy-layer" {
    source = "./modules/policy-layer"
    k8s_cluster = var.cluster_name
    egress_allowlist = var.egress_allowlist # cidrs and ports
    egress_mirror_policy = var.egress_mirror_policy # selectors + sample rate
  }

Important TF patterns and gotchas:
- Keep mirror subnets separate and tag them for retention/compliance review.
- Firewall rules must explicitly allow collector IPs to receive mirrored flows from worker subnets.
- Use IAM roles + VPC endpoint policies for collector ingest (to avoid exposing ports publicly).
- Don't rely on global default route tables; create explicit routing for mirror overlay to ensure mirrored traffic never leaves customer VPC unless explicitly permitted.
- When refactoring existing TF, maintain backward compatibility via module wrappers (inputs that map old variables) to reduce churn for existing integrations.

Network policy considerations (k8s):
- Add a Namespaced EgressMirror CRD for enabling mirroring on a per-namespace or per-pod basis (selectors). This avoids cluster-wide toggles and supports canary by namespace.
- Default: disabled for system namespaces (kube-system, redwood-system).
- The egress mirroring controller annotates pod iptables/eBPF sampler with sampling rate.

Firewall / Perimeter rules checklist:
- Worker -> Collector (UDP/TCP depending on encapsulation) on ports 9000/9001 allowed.
- Collector -> Observability only from mirror-subnet CIDRs; no inbound from internet.
- NAT fallback must not introduce hairpin NAT into internal services (validate with tests).
- Logging: firewall hits to collector ports must be captured in flow logs for 30 days during canary.

DNS handling and split-horizon notes:
- Use a private hosted zone under customer DNS (collector.internal.redwood) and create resolver conditional forwarding rules if customer manages their own DNS.
- Terraform should offer a boolean var "use_customer_dns" which toggles whether we create records or emit resolution instructions for customer teams.
- When changing private DNS records, always stage in a lower TTL (60s) then increase after 24–72 hours of stability.

Observability and telemetry gating:
- Telemetry events to check before increasing sample rate: mirror queue depth, packet loss % at collector, CPU on worker nodes, additional TCP retries observed by app logs.
- Gate: if collector packet loss > 0.5% for 1m, automatically reduce sample rate by 50% until stable.
- Metrics to emit: mirror_sample_rate{namespace,pod}, mirror_drop_rate, collector_ingest_latency_ms, mirror_queue_depth.

Rollout plan (canary-first):
1) Unit testing of eBPF program in cluster-lab.
2) Deploy TF modules to staging VPC with mirror_enabled = true, sample_rate = 0.002 (0.2%).
3) Enable for a single non-critical namespace in staging. Observe 72h.
4) Deploy to one low-risk prod customer (customer A) as a 0.5% canary. Collect increased telemetry retention for 14 days.
5) If stable, increment sample to 1% and expand to a second prod customer (customer B).
6) After 30 days of stable metrics, consider 2% and wider rollout.

Rollback / mitigation strategies:
- Immediate: flip module variable mirror_enabled = false and run terraform apply (fast path).
- Mid-term: scale collector replicas to 0 to stop ingest and cause sampler to backpressure (sampler should default to drop-only, preserving original flow).
- Long-term: revert TF module refactor with wrapper modules if any regressions observed in networking behavior.

Testing & validation checklist (pre-apply and post-apply):
Pre-apply:
- iptables/iproute2/eBPF tooling present on worker images (kernel versions supported list).
- PR: terraform plan approved by infra + security.
- Conformance tests for sampler under load in lab cluster (10k concurrent connections).

Post-apply quick checks:
- dig @resolver collector.internal.redwood => returns collector IPs (if TF created records).
- tcpdump -n -i any host <collector_ip> and verify encapsulated packets from worker nodes (sampling rate sanity).
- curl -sS --resolve example.com:443:<dest-ip> ... validate original flows unaffected.
- netcat/ss to collector ports from worker nodes to confirm firewall rules.

Operational runbook snippets (quick commands):
- Check mirror sampler status: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l app=egress-sampler
- Check collector logs: kubectl -n observability logs deployment/mirror-collector -f --since=1h
- Verify sample rate metrics: curl "http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=mirror_sample_rate" | jq .
- Force reduce sample rate via k8s annotation: kubectl annotate ns my-canary redwood.io/mirror-rate=0.005 --overwrite

Security & compliance notes:
- By default, collectors must run in a restricted VPC with no egress to public internet.
- Mirroring must honor tenant isolation: do not mix mirrored traffic from multiple customers in the same collector unless tenant tagging and retention policies are enforced.
- Submit data handling checklist to security@redwood before enabling for any customer.

Migration & refactor timeline (6–8 weeks suggested):
- Week 1–2: implement TF module skeleton, tests, and eBPF prototype.
- Week 3: internal lab validation and code review PRs.
- Week 4: staging rollout + telemetry validation.
- Week 5–6: initial customer canaries + iter on metrics/alerts.
- Week 7–8: wider rollout and TF module deprecation of legacy resources.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we permit optional proxying of mirrored traffic back into NAT path for on-prem environments where device-level sampling is unavailable? (security wants clear controls)
- Default sample rate policy: should it be org-wide 0.5% or per-customer opt-in?
- Retention policy for mirrored metadata vs payload: where to store it and who can access?

References and links:
- confluence:private-deploy-networking-overview-8732
- github PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/246
- Jira: NETOPS-412 (egress mirroring epic)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative; the design favors not impacting production flows over capturing 100% of egress.
- Look for missing edge cases: air-gapped installs, legacy TF users who assume single shared route table, and customer-managed DNS constraints.

Next steps (action items):
- Marcus: create TF module repo skeleton and open initial PR (due 2026-02-28).
- Ruth: prototype eBPF sampler in lab and document kernel compatibility matrix (due 2026-03-05).
- Kai: draft security data handling checklist and circulate to legal (due 2026-03-03).
- Aisha: schedule canary customers and draft customer opt-in notice (due 2026-03-10).

Version history:

- v0.2 (2026-03-08) clarified rollback paths and added telemetry gating thresholds.
